Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some pianos are guitars.

All guitars are flutes.

**Conclusion:**

I) Some pianos are flute.

II) No guitar is a piano.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow.
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some pianos are guitars.

All guitars are flutes.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d36cd4a8702d4864275cd0569183b99cb99921847ac19a1726d4326bb02de6d6.png] 

Conclusion:

I) Some pianos are flute - True (Some pianos are guitars and all guitars are flutes implies that some pianos are flute)

II) No guitar is a piano - False (Some pianos are guitars implies also that some guitars are definitely piano)

So, only Conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Option 1) 15, 40

Given: 30 × 6 ÷ 15 + 7 + 40 = 50

After interchanging the numbers we get:

⇒ 30 × __**6 ÷ 40**__ + 7 + 15 = 50

⇒ __**30 × (3 / 20)**__ + 7 + 15 = 50

⇒ (__**9/2) + 7 + 15**__ = 50

⇒ (53 / 2) ≠ 50

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are of different heights. A is shorter than only three people. D is taller than only F. B is taller than A but shorter than both C and E. E is not the tallest person. How many people are shorter than G?
questions.solution:
**Given: **A, B, C, D, E, F and G are of different heights.

1) A is shorter than only three people.

2) D is taller than only F.

⇒ _ > _ > _ > A >_ > D > F. 

3) B is taller than A but shorter than both C and E.

4)E is not the tallest person.

5) Only one place is vacant which is occupied by G.

⇒ C > E > B > A > > G > D > F. 

Thus, only** two **people are shorter than G.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2".**

⇒ 26 × 2 + 1 ≠ 53.

Hence, the correct option is "Option (2)".

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All watches are cameras.

No camera is a pen.

Some watches are balls.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some balls are cameras.

II. No ball is a pen.

III. No pen is a watch.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All watches are cameras.

No camera is a pen.

Some watches are balls.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d5e0dd039e18da64a666f61a389cbff4520e3eaf3fe7abad8a83c7630ce7f33.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some balls are cameras. - True (It is given that some watches are balls and all watches are cameras, so, the balls which is watches is also cameras).

II. No ball is a pen - False (There is Not any definite relation is given between ball and pen, so it can be possible only).

III. No pen is a watch - **True** (It is given that all watches are cameras and no camera is pen, so, watches are also not pen).

So, Both conclusions I and III follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number.

15 ∶ 145 ∶∶ 10 ∶ 95 ∶∶ 20 ∶ ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number × 9) + (1st number - 5) = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 15 ∶ 145

⇒ (15 × 9 ) + (15 - 5)

⇒ 135 + 10 = 145.

For, 10 ∶ 95

⇒ (10 × 9 ) + (10 - 5)

⇒ 90 + 5 = 95.

Similarly, for 20 ∶ ?

⇒ (20 × 9) + (20 - 5)

⇒ 180 + 15 = 195.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
